key_insight: Weight-streaming decode activates every weight row each 20-50 ms token, inside the 32-64 ms window, so refreshing those rows is redundant; a coverage bitmap makes skipping safe.
killer_doubt: Gain caps at the refresh tax on weight rows only (~5-10% bandwidth); KV, activations, OS pages and idle servers still need refresh, so the engine cannot leave the die.
decisive_experiment: Replay vLLM decode traces in Ramulator 2 with per-row last-activation times; measure the share of rows touched within 32 ms and the bandwidth recovered by skipping their REFs. ~$30k.
prior_art: Smart Refresh (Ghosh and Lee, MICRO 2007) skips recently accessed rows; RANA (ISCA 2018) skips eDRAM refresh using DNN data lifetime [training knowledge].

key_insight: One leaky analog integrator per 4 rows counts every activation with no counter table, no in-array read-modify-write and no many-sided evasion; ~3T+1C per 4 rows fits the driver strip.
killer_doubt: A leakage-set 64 ms time constant drifts ~2x per 10-15 C and packet mismatch adds tens of %; trip spread beyond ~2x over 0-95 C breaks a 500-versus-1k margin.
decisive_experiment: 65 nm MPW with 1k integrators using a bias-referenced (PTAT) leaker; measure trip-count distribution from 0 to 95 C and under pulse-width variation. Pass: 6-sigma spread under 2x. ~$150k.
prior_art: Digital counters: JEDEC DDR5 PRAC, Graphene, ABACuS; LIRMM decaying 'forgetful' counters; no analog charge-integrator counter found (via search snippet).

key_insight: A precision-select column command lets one stored tensor serve 4-, 8- or 16-bit reads, moving only needed planes; useful for adaptive-precision KV scoring, not static quantized weights.
killer_doubt: Static quantization already stores 4-bit weights, so the 2-4x appears only for dynamically varying precision, likely under 20% of decode traffic, and it needs a JEDEC die change.
decisive_experiment: GPU software emulation: bit-plane KV with MSB-first scoring (Any-Precision style); measure bytes moved and accuracy versus INT4/INT8 on long-context tasks. Pursue a die change only if over 2x. ~$40k.
prior_art: Any-Precision LLM (ICML 2024) bit-plane weights; SIMDRAM/Ambit vertical layouts; Fine-Grained DRAM (NVIDIA, MICRO 2017) partial activation [training knowledge].

key_insight: Circulating charge loops sensed by one floating-diffusion amp per 64 packets need no per-bit transistor, capacitor or wordline, and buried channels give seconds of retention.
killer_doubt: At CIS-fab F~45 nm a 2F2 packet is ~4,000 nm2, ~4.7x DRAM's 864 nm2 cell; clocking all gates at 4 GHz costs ~0.2 W per Mb at 0.05 fF/gate.
decisive_experiment: Fabricate 64-stage buried-channel CCD loops at minimum gate pitch on a CIS shuttle; measure transfer efficiency at 1-4 GHz, full well per um2 and clock power per bit. ~$300k.
prior_art: 1970s CCD memories (Fairchild, Intel 2416); imec IGZO CCD buffer memory, IEDM 2024 and 3D at IMW 2026 (via search snippet, R01 log).

key_insight: Shifting charge between two coupled MOS gates and back reads a well non-destructively, allowing averaged multi-sample sensing with no restore and X-Y select without a per-cell transistor.
killer_doubt: A 4F2 surface well (F=20 nm) holds ~110 e-: ~0.2 mV on a 100 fF column; 85 C surface generation fills it in under 0.5 s; writes need a diffusion.
decisive_experiment: Build CID gate-pair arrays with 16-cell column segments on a 180 nm CIS shuttle; measure controlled-injection write accuracy, column signal and dark fill time at 85 C. ~$150k.
prior_art: GE CID imagers (1970s); Fossum QIS jots; 1970s CCD memories [training knowledge]; no CID-as-RAM found.

key_insight: Decoupled sense amps can latch a row without developing the bitlines; for data truly dead after one read, the restore swing, the largest activation term, can be skipped.
killer_doubt: KV cache is re-read every token, not once; for row-aligned streams activation is ~0.1-0.3 pJ/bit versus 3-20 pJ/bit I/O, so system energy falls under ~5%.
decisive_experiment: Instrument LLM training and inference traces for the share of HBM bytes read exactly once and row-aligned; model savings in DRAMPower. Build only if over 30% of bytes and 10% energy. ~$40k.
prior_art: Destructive-read DRAM with write-back buffers (2000s); restore truncation (HPCA 2016); bitline-isolation sense amps are standard [training knowledge].

key_insight: Dies that fail sense margin only when hot are usable in liquid-cooled racks held under 60 C; a temperature-graded SKU turns some yield loss into salable bits.
killer_doubt: Hot-only sense fails are likely ~1-3% of dies after redundancy, not 3-8%; temperature grades and downgraded parts already exist, and cooling excursions add field risk.
decisive_experiment: With a test house, bin 10k reject DDR5 dies by failing temperature; measure the share passing JEDEC timing at or below 60 C through 1,000 h burn-in. ~$100k.
prior_art: Commercial versus industrial temperature grades; Micron SpecTek downgraded components; routine speed and temperature binning [training knowledge].

key_insight: Retired DDR4 is wafer-free capacity; an FPGA CXL card with retention profiling and chipkill makes it a trusted slow tier at ~10-20% of new cost/bit during a 4x price spike.
killer_doubt: Already shipping: Marvell Structera X and Microsoft GreenSKU reuse DDR4 over CXL; the retired DDR4 pool is finite and shrinks as fleets move to DDR5.
decisive_experiment: As strategy only: buy 500 retired RDIMMs, profile retention and BER on an FPGA CXL card, and price the tier against new DDR5 contracts. ~$100k.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X DDR4-capable CXL controller; ITAD resale markets [training knowledge, consistent with other R-batch reviews].

key_insight: Same mechanism as I-03344, but as a buffer ASIC with in-situ per-row retention profiling and per-region refresh; the water and fab-avoidance argument is real.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-03344 and of shipping CXL controllers; a new buffer ASIC needs over $10M in masks and IP, ten times the budget.
decisive_experiment: FPGA CXL card profiling 500 retired DIMMs; justify an ASIC only if per-row refresh tuning adds over 20% usable capacity versus simple binning. ~$100k.
prior_art: Marvell Structera X; Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); REAPER/AVATAR retention profiling [training knowledge].

key_insight: SA resolution time encodes |dV|; flagging slow decisions turns margin errors into erasures at half the parity cost, so ECC-paid capacitors (N-62) shrink further or refresh stretches 2-4x.
killer_doubt: If most raw errors at 1e-4 are confident flips (VRT, fully leaked cells) rather than small-|dV| ones, under ~50% get flagged; a per-SA flag latch adds ~3-5% die.
decisive_experiment: DRAM Bender on 50 DDR4/DDR5 chips: read rows at nominal and reduced tRCD as a flag proxy, then at stretched refresh measure the fraction of errors flagged. Pass: over 80%. ~$60k.
prior_art: Static weak-cell erasure maps (US 8,898,544); Solar-DRAM reduced-tRCD weak profiles (via search snippet); NAND soft-decision LDPC; IBM chipkill chip marking.

key_insight: An unpatterned charge film addressed by a CMOS-driven field-emitter array removes per-bit transistors and lines; only a relaxed ~200 nm emitter grid needs patterning.
killer_doubt: Each tip needs its own 8 nm-focusing lens and 64x64 deflection, beyond multi-beam litho tools; beam writes through nitride are fluence-limited to ~1e2-1e5 cycles (C0-2) versus ~1e13.
decisive_experiment: Write and read 8-16 nm charge dots in a nitride film with an SEM, cycling one site 1e8 times to measure endurance and beam-induced read current. ~$80k.
prior_art: GE/Control Data EBAM/BEAMOS (1970s); HP Atomic Resolution Storage field-emitter storage (~2000); IBM Millipede probe storage [training knowledge].

key_insight: Avalanche gain turns a ~100-electron packet into a full-swing digital event, so the storage node could be a planar diffusion if dark counts and leakage were negligible.
killer_doubt: A 0.02 fF node (~125 e-) drains in ~20 ms at a 1 fA junction-leakage tail; CMOS SPAD breakdown is ~10-25 V, far above the 3 V wordline floor.
decisive_experiment: On a 180 nm SPAD-capable shuttle, couple a gated diffusion to a SPAD; measure trigger probability for 0 versus 100 injected electrons, plus dark-count and afterpulse errors at 85 C. ~$150k.
prior_art: Z-RAM impact-ionisation floating body; EMCCD gain registers; Fossum QIS reads single electrons without avalanche [training knowledge]; similar idea I-05065 dropped elsewhere.
